phases.title: Survival
phases.goal: Read Hangul confidently and handle basic greetings, numbers, and polite requests.
can: Read and write all 14 basic consonants and 10 vowels of Hangul, plus common batchim (final consonants)
Use 안녕하세요, 감사합니다, 죄송합니다 and other core polite set phrases
Count with both native (하나, 둘, 셋) and Sino-Korean (일, 이, 삼) numbers and know when to use each
Build simple SOV sentences with the polite -아/어요 ending (가요, 먹어요, 있어요)
Attach the topic 은/는 and subject 이/가 particles to nouns correctly
Order food and ask 얼마예요? / 이거 주세요 in a shop or restaurant
phases.daily: 10 min Hangul reading drills, 10 min learning 5 new words, 5 min repeating survival phrases aloud, 5 min number practice.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.goal: Speak in past, present, and future about everyday life using core particles and negation.
can: Conjugate the past tense with -았/었어요 and future intention with -(으)ㄹ 거예요
Negate sentences two ways: 안 + verb and verb stem + -지 않아요
Use the object 을/를 and location particles 에 (static) vs 에서 (action)
Tell time mixing native-number hours (세 시) and Sino-number minutes (삼십 분)
Handle descriptive verbs (adjectives) like 좋아요, 비싸요 that conjugate like verbs
Ask and answer questions with 뭐, 어디, 언제, 왜, 누구, 어떻게
phases.daily: 15 min verb conjugation practice, 10 min listening to a beginner podcast, 10 min writing 3 sentences, 5 min flashcards.

phases.title: Core Structures
phases.goal: Connect clauses and express ability, desire, obligation, and comparison in natural speech.
can: Link ideas with connectives -고 (and), -아/어서 (so/because), -지만 (but)
Express ability with -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 and desire with -고 싶다
State obligation (-아/어야 되다), permission (-아/어도 되다), and prohibition (-지 마세요)
Form conditionals with -(으)면 and progressive actions with -고 있어요
Compare things with 보다 + 더 and form superlatives with 가장/제일
Use the honorific -(으)시- and honorific words (드시다, 계시다) to show respect
phases.daily: 20 min grammar workbook, 15 min speaking with a tutor or app, 10 min reading short dialogues, 10 min vocabulary review.

phases.title: Fluency
phases.goal: Handle relative clauses, reported speech, and irregular verbs across varied topics.
can: Build noun-modifying (relative) clauses with -(으)ㄴ / -는 / -(으)ㄹ endings
Master the ㅂ, ㄷ, 르, ㅅ, and ㄹ irregular verb stems in speech
Report what others said with -다고/-라고 하다 and its contractions (-대요)
Nominalize verbs with -는 것 and -기 to talk about activities and ideas
Switch between the -아/어요 polite style and the -습니다 formal style appropriately
Follow and join native-paced conversations on daily topics like news and travel
phases.daily: 20 min native media (K-drama or YouTube) with Korean subtitles, 15 min shadowing, 15 min writing a journal entry, 10 min reviewing irregulars.

phases.title: Mastery
phases.goal: Communicate with nuance, appropriate speech levels, and cultural fluency in any setting.
can: Choose the right speech level (반말, 해요체, 하십시오체) for each social situation
Use nuanced endings like -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 (conjecture) and -(으)려고/-(으)러 (intention/purpose) naturally
Understand Sino-Korean vocabulary roots (한자어) to guess advanced words
Express favors and benefactive nuance with -아/어 주다 / 드리다
Read newspapers, essays, and web content, and write formal emails or reports
Adjust honorifics and humble forms fluidly to match age and status of the listener
phases.daily: 30 min reading authentic articles or novels, 20 min conversation on abstract topics, 15 min writing formal texts, 10 min noting new idioms and 한자어.
